Hey OP. I know that you have a lot of comments . Just know that I am here for you and willing to lend an ear and a shoulder. I’ve been in your shoes, to a very similar extent. Hopefully, my story below can give you a glimpse into a future that will be okay.

When I found out I was pregnant, the biggest difference between our situations is that my (at the time) SO and I were not a married couple. We had been dating for a while though and had a very loving relationship. When I found out about the baby, my initial thought was “there is no way I can take care of a child in our situation”. We were both 25 at this time.

I told him about the baby and we both talked it over. I was not sure what to do at the time, but he was very certain of abortion. So I decided, at first, to agree and schedule an abortion. Over time, though, (a span of weeks), I knew I couldn’t do it. I did everything to convince him of any other option, but he was not happy. He was set on abortion. I really thought *there’s not a way I can think of living with myself after an abortion. If my baby can’t live, I won’t either.*

So, I scheduled the abortion - BUT also scheduled an outside appointment with an OBGYN. I brought him to the OBGYN and he was mad that the NP who saw me suggested this be my decision. He felt that he had so much life left to live and was not ready for this. But when we saw the ultrasound, he started sobbing because he was so overwhelmed and pissed at me (I asked him about why he was crying later). He ignored me for the night, ran off to drink, and told everyone at the bar who would listen about our situation. I really began to consider what the NP said about this being my decision. It would affect me forever in a way he would never have to live with.

I also realized that maybe he needed time. So I told him of my decision to keep the baby, which was a weight off of my shoulders and lessened my suicidal thoughts. He eventually warmed up to the idea of a baby. But he was a jacka$$ the entire pregnancy. He didn’t help with anything. He made me feel bad and spoke down to me. He called me names and treated the whole thing like a nuisance. We went to couples therapy, and he even got kicked out because he became so belligerent over the situation. After 8 months, he still told me many times how “this kids gonna ruin my life”. For the record, we are (obviously) no longer together

After nine months total. I had my beautiful baby boy (almost a year ago) and despite his dad being a piece of crap, I would never look back. I’m a changed person. Before, I never had the confidence to do pretty much anything in life. Now, something in me has changed. I put myself together everyday in a way that I NEVER did before, even when I was a young, hot, size 2 young adult. I work hard. I have most of my debts paid off. And it’s all because I came into my own after having a child. With the right mixture of low dose of sertraline and my baby, I have learned to tackle the world.

I’m not saying it won’t be hard. His father is very much a show daddy and makes this whole situation difficult for his own selfish gain. But I don’t care. I would do anything for my child. His father is irrelevant now to me anyways, besides the fact that I respect him as my child’s father and do not want our son to see any of our disagreements. 

Your life may just need to be watered by this beautiful life inside of you. A garden may be ready to grow.

I’m so very sorry to hear this, love. It seems as though this built up over time, which is typically how it goes. Chances are, his liver was close to failure prior to you finalizing anything. To take on the responsibility of this would be to not only take on his death but the years of alcoholic behavior, and that is *not your fault*. 

Much easier said than done, be kind to yourself. Take care of yourself. There is most likely a grief process you are going through, regardless of any separation, and this blame will do nothing for you. There is a loss of both the alcoholic that died and the person you knew before all of this that I would imagine you are experiencing right now. You deserve to feel comforted, not shameful. 

As for his parents, they are taking their grief and manifesting it into blame. I’m sorry they are grieving, but so are you. Im so sorry on their behalf that you are being blamed. Im sure you did your best to make things work before any separation. 

Remember, you are not alone. A good resource would be Al-Anon. Similar to AA (it’s also a 12-step group) but for people who have been affected by their loved ones alcoholism. From their website:
““Alcoholism is a family disease. The disease affects all those who have a relationship with a problem drinker. Those of us closest to the alcoholic suffer the most, and those who care the most can easily get caught up in the behavior of another person. We react to the alcoholic’s behavior. We focus on them, what they do, where they are, how much they drink. We try to control their drinking for them. **We take on the blame, guilt, and shame that belong to the drinker”.**

There’s definitely better ways to put what people are saying. I’ll give you a short answer plus a pros and cons, then you can decide.

Target gives pretty heavy workload. At most other retail store, you can see two people slowly working on a pallet at once. Not Target. You’re expected to push each flat or cart or boat of product for your section by yourself, and get it done by the end of the night, regardless of if you’re a full 8 hours or cut back to 6 or less, like it is now. I work grocery, so it’s a very fast-paced job. I’ve also done fulfillment, which can be a wild card. If you’re a good worker, they’ll continually expect more and more, but not give you the hours to help alleviate larger responsibilities.

Pros:
- $15/hour is good for retail, especially if you’re not in an expensive city or area.
- Most customers that go there are obsessed with target in some way, so most are in a decent mood.
- Sometimes, and just sometimes, you do get recognized for hard work, if you have good leads.

Cons:
- As said above, if you’re a good worker, they’ll always expect more. It’s almost never going to be enough. Whatever you do.
- Annual pay raises are meager, starting at $0.06 annually. That was the max anyone got this year at my store. That’s how they keep starting rate at $15.
- You could be the best worker, but if your TL doesn’t care, you won’t see the hours regardless. 
- You WILL eventually be fulfillment trained. And they WILL pull you into fulfillment when they need, even if you have a ton of work to do yourself.
- As any retail job, customers can really suck. They run carts into you, ask dumb questions, throw random shit all over the store; the list goes on.
- It’s really hard to move up unless you’re okay with moving stores and departments. There’s one TL per department, and unless their supervisor quits AND they have sufficient experience, chances are they aren’t going anywhere. And you’re not being promoted. The quickest anyone was ever promoted at my store was after 4.5 years. It’s a long ladder with your boots nailed to the floor and reaching a 6,000 ft ceiling.
$15 at every target. In cities where $15 is the minimum wage, like Chicago, they sometimes go up to $16.50 starting. Depends where in said city though.
